races.title: State House, District 13
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jason Moore
cands.bio: Insurance agency owner and NC State graduate (2001) who grew up in Hurdle Mills. His 20-plus-year career spans insurance, real estate and farming. He was the Democratic nominee for NC House District 13 (Carteret and Craven counties) in 2026. No prior elected office is documented.

endorsements.text: North Carolina Association of Educators (listed among his endorsements on Ballotpedia)

cands.gaps: We found no record of Jason Moore holding any elected or appointed office, so there is no voting or legislative record to report. We found no documented actions in office. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B visas, policing, gun laws, or abortion. His birth year and the date he moved to Carteret or Craven County were not found. His birthplace and upbringing come only from his campaign website. No controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond the education association were found.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Hurdle Mills, NC, and Ballotpedia lists a Person High School diploma and an NC State degree, which is consistent with that; the birthplace claim itself comes only from the campaign site.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owns an insurance agency and has worked over 20 years across insurance, real estate and farming; no legislative or other elected office is documented.
qual.why: He is a business owner with a long work record, which fits the middle band; no legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found.
qual.label: He is a business owner with a long work record, which fits the middle band; no legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He pledges on his campaign site to fight for teacher pay and to defend public schools; he does not address vouchers, charters or school choice there.

cands.name: Celeste Cairns
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 13 (Carteret County and part of Craven County) since 2023. Former CPA with Deloitte, with audit and consulting work at Willis Corroon and HCA Healthcare. Ran in the 2019 special Republican primary for NC-3. Lives in Emerald Isle.
cands.gaps: We could not find when Celeste Cairns moved to North Carolina or where she grew up. The pages we read did not show which bills she sponsored or any specific actions in office on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Her stated positions come from a 2019 congressional campaign website and a general statement on her current campaign site. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any cycle. We found no documented statements on data centers or development, no controversies, no foreign ties and no endorsements.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2023. Earlier worked as a CPA with Deloitte and in audit and consulting at Willis Corroon Corporation and HCA Healthcare Corporation; earned a business administration degree from the University of Georgia.
qual.why: Prior legislative service (re-elected in 2024 and 2026) plus a professional accounting, audit and consulting career fits a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: Prior legislative service (re-elected in 2024 and 2026) plus a professional accounting, audit and consulting career fits a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee seats were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Said on her 2019 congressional campaign website that she is '100%, unapologetically pro-life' and would fight to defund Planned Parenthood; she also said she sits on the board of a local pregnancy resource center.

second-amendment.evidence: Said on her 2019 congressional campaign website that she is a gun owner and NRA member who would fight any attempt to take away Second Amendment rights.
